The U.S. Constitution is the supreme law, and under the Supremacy Clause any treaty, federal statute, or state law that conflicts with it is invalid. Below it, federal treaties and statutes are coequal (the later-in-time one controls), followed by federal regulations, then state constitutions, state statutes, state regulations, and local ordinances. Valid federal law overrides conflicting state law, and the place of common law varies by context.

CONFIDENCE: 85
